title: TWA — the original corporate-raid playbook
statement: Icahn accumulated control of Trans World Airlines and extracted hundreds of millions through asset sales, buybacks at premium prices and finally a leveraged buyout — the template for the 1980s raider reputation.
outcome: Icahn profited enormously; TWA was later sold to American Airlines and its employees suffered massively, an outcome labor advocates cite against him to this day.

title: Texaco-Getty fight and the Pennzoil windfall
statement: Icahn bought a large Texaco stake after a Pennsylvania jury imposed a $10.5 billion judgment on Texaco for interfering with Pennzoil's Getty acquisition, arguing the companies would settle far below par.
outcome: Texaco entered bankruptcy protection and settled for $3 billion; the stock recovered and Icahn's position — and his greenmail premium in the settlement — produced hundreds of millions in profit.

title: Founding Icahn Enterprises as a public holding company
statement: Icahn organized his holdings into a public vehicle, giving him permanent capital and public-company currency for his campaigns.
outcome: Icahn Enterprises became his permanent activist platform; its dividend and valuation performance have been mixed, but it has funded four decades of campaigns.

title: Apple — pushing the buyback in dinner with Tim Cook
statement: Icahn built a multi-billion dollar Apple position and pressed Tim Cook directly for a much larger buyback, arguing the market was pricing a great franchise as if it were a fading hardware maker.
outcome: Apple expanded its buyback to become history's largest capital-return program; Icahn exited in 2016 ahead of the stock's greatest run, a sale he later called premature.

title: eBay — the PayPal separation campaign
statement: Icahn bought into eBay and publicly demanded the separation of PayPal, arguing the two businesses had no synergy and that management was protecting its own scope.
outcome: eBay spun PayPal off in 2015; the payment company created far more value standalone than analysts predicted, validating the separation logic.

title: Herbalife — the long side of the Ackman war
statement: Icahn took the opposite side of Ackman's billion-dollar short, buying a large long stake with board representation, partly on valuation analysis and famously partly on personal animus.
outcome: The stock's rise squeezed the short; Icahn's stake roughly quintupled, he called it one of his best investments ever, and the position was later reduced in 2023.
